history.period: Early 8th century CE (origins; 8th-century inscription in situ)
history.summary: Active living Shiva temple on the banks of the Mahanadi at Sirpur, Mahasamund district. Built in the early 8th century CE (per Outlook Traveller); the present structure is generally believed to be a reconstruction of the older original, and the temple is routinely re-washed and re-painted, so it has lost much of its antique appearance. The courtyard and premises hold recovered sculptures over a thousand years old — Hindu, Buddhist and Jain iconography including a black-rock Buddha in bhumisparsha mudra, Chamunda, Mahishasuramardini, Gangadhara Shiva, Nataraja, Uma-Maheshvara, Vishnu, Trimurti and Navagraha. A stone slab in the temple wall carries a Sanskrit inscription in Nagari script dedicated to Shiva, dated to the 8th century CE. Annual religious fair held here coinciding with Shivratri. CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the district/town name 'Mahasamund' — corrected to Chhattisgarh; actual town is Sirpur.

name: Gandheshwar Temple
town_description: Sirpur (ancient Shripura/Sripura) is a historic town on the banks of the Mahanadi in Mahasamund district, Chhattisgarh, about 82 km from Raipur. Capital of Dakshina Kosala from the 5th to 12th century CE, it is a multireligious archaeological site — Hindu temples, Buddhist viharas and Jain viharas side by side — being prepared for a UNESCO World Heritage bid.

travel.road: On NH 53, ~82 km from Raipur and ~37 km from Mahasamund town; regular bus services connect Raipur and Sirpur

visitor_information.opening_hours: Active temple with regular poojas; no published hours — verify locally
